family_difference: Heading is the same flat printing at the four larger steps (display, headline, title, emphasis), always medium weight and primary ink, rendered as a real h1 to h4 so the outline of a page is in the markup.
concept: Heading is the name printed largest on a unit or a page. It uses the same grotesk and grey ink as the rest of the case, and it is louder only by size and by sitting first on the inset line.

root.why: A heading prints in medium weight and primary ink with tight leading, never bold and never tinted.

l1.why: Level one is the display step for the single page title, tracked in slightly at that size.

l2.why: Level two is the headline step that names a section of a page, such as a room.

l3.why: Level three is the title step that names one unit, printed on its top inset line.

l4.why: Level four is the emphasis step for a group inside a unit or a sheet.
